title: Decouple batch retimer and implement compact flusher for KV coherency
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The continuous batching controller and KV cache compaction currently share a synchronous timing/retimer path inside the scheduler thread. This coupling leads to periodic p99 tail spikes when the compaction/flush path runs inline with slot arbitration or when bursty checkpoint work interacts with the batch commit window. We also see sharp memory churn during large compaction runs which temporarily increases GC pressure in the host process and causes upstream request backpressure.

Goal: Reduce tail latency and memory churn by decoupling the batch retimer from the scheduler hot path and moving compact/flush work to a bounded, cooperative flusher worker. The work should maintain KV coherency guarantees for in-flight sessions and preserve correctness of lease/heartbeat semantics.

Scope / What we'll deliver:
- Extract a light-weight BatchRetimer actor that only signals batch deadlines and never runs compaction work inline.
- Introduce a CompactFlusher subsystem: a background worker pool with backpressure tokens and per-shard compact windows.
- Replace the synchronous compaction loop with incremental compaction slices so pauses are short and preemptible.
- Add lease-aware coordination so inflight sessions keep higher priority and flusher slices avoid touching hot KV slots.
- Metrics and dashboards: per-shard compaction progress, flusher queue length, slice duration, and p50/p95/p99 request latency correlated with compaction activity.

Design notes:
- Use an MPSC ring for BatchRetimer -> scheduler signals to avoid lock contention. Retimer only emits deadline events and a lightweight hint for prioritization.
- CompactFlusher will implement a token-bucket to limit concurrent slices and a soft-priority that prefers cold shards first (based on last-accessed timestamp histogram).
- Compaction slices are interruptible: each slice must check an epoch/lease guard to ensure it does not compact keys needed by an active session. The epoch guard is implemented as an atomic epoch counter per-shard.
- Avoid full mutex protection across scheduler and flusher by using per-shard atomic markers and a small compare-and-swap protocol for slice ownership.

Migration / rollout plan:
1) Spike and benchmarks in a dev cluster with synthetic mixed-length sessions.
2) Dark-launch CompactFlusher toggled via config flag; measure background CPU and memory.
3) Canary on a single region (5% traffic) with metrics alarms on p99 and error rate.
4) Full rollout if no regressions after 48 hours; otherwise iterate.

Acceptance criteria:
- No functional regression: all existing unit/integration tests pass.
- p99 latency for short chat requests reduces or remains stable under same load when compared to baseline under compaction-heavy workload. Target: p99 <= baseline + 5% during compaction.
- Memory churn (RSS growth during a 10-minute compaction window) reduced by >=25% in the Canary run.
- Dashboards for compaction slice metrics are live and alert on slice > 200ms.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: incorrect epoch coordination leads to stale key compaction and session errors. Mitigation: add extensive unit tests around epoch guards, and a fail-open flag that pauses flusher if any lease anomalies are detected.
- Risk: flusher CPU competes with inference; mitigation: flusher runs on lower niceness and honors GPU-executor CPU reservations; also make concurrency adaptive based on host load.

Dependencies: ENG-842371 (scheduler healing), ENG-214365 (commit-coordinator cleanup), runtime lib bump to 3.1.2 for atomic epoch helpers.

Testing plan:
- New unit tests for slice interrupt semantics and epoch guards.
- Integration test: simulate long-lived sessions + compaction churn and verify no data races via ThreadSanitizer run on CI job.
- Perf job: automated benchmark comparing baseline vs decoupled flusher under a mixed workload.

Docs and follow-ups:
- Confluence doc with sequence diagrams and failure modes (link below).
- Follow-up ticket to consider persistent compaction checkpointing to reduce repeated work on cold shards.
